reading.body:
IAD37 publishes 500 MW of IT capacity, making it the largest single campus by declared load among 19 Virginia facilities tracked here, and it accounts for roughly 38 percent of the 1,326 MW published across those 19 facilities.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities in total, but the vast majority publish no capacity figure. The state's true installed base is larger than what the numbers here reflect. This opacity matters for grid planning, since neither operators nor regulators have a complete picture of aggregate demand in one of the country's densest data center regions.

At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 500 MW of IT load translates to roughly 12,500 racks and approximately 1.25 million accelerator slots across the campus. At 10 kW per rack, a legacy enterprise density, the same power supports 50,000 racks. Digital Realty does not publish a rack count or per-rack power envelope, so the actual composition of its load remains opaque. Which tenants occupy the campus and what fraction of capacity is committed versus available are also undisclosed.

The facility holds three certifications: PCI DSS for payment card workloads, ISO 27001 for information security management, and ISO 9001 for quality processes. These qualifications signal what workload types the operator permits, but not what workloads actually run there or how the 500 MW distributes among them.
